newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 8.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 8.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Gold prices slumped again overnight in the wake of the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to sell 60 percent of its gold holdings. The bullion price sagged to a brief 12 year low of US$313.90 in London before bouncing back to be trading at US$318 in late New York trade. Some dealers, however, said Monday afternoon's selloff may have been overdone.

Mt Leyshon Gold Mines Ltd said on Monday its gold production rose four percent to 219,106 ounces for the 12 months ended June 30. Fourth quarter gold production totalled 59,233 ounces. Total cash costs for the year decreased 9.1 percent to A$330 per ounce while total cash costs for the quarter were 2.1 percent lower than in the previous quarter at A$320 per ounce.
Coal and Allied's attempt to use non-union labour to load up a coal train and bypass a union picket line at its strike-bound Hunter Valley Number One mine remained stalled on Monday afternoon.

Production tests at the Singa-1 well in South Sumatra were in line with gas reserve estimates of about 500 billion cubic feet (bcf), analysts said on Monday. Operator Energy Equity Corp Ltd earlier reported production testing at the exploration well had confirmed a new field gas discovery, with a flow of 20.3 million cubic feet per day over 12-1/4 hours through a 40/64 inch choke.
